paper.title: The KL-UCB Algorithm for Bounded Stochastic Bandits and Beyond

settings.name_in_paper: Stochastic bandit with K arms and independent rewards bounded in [0,1]
settings.definition_quote: the set of actions is $\{1,\dots,K\}$, where $K$ denotes a finite integer. For each $a\in\{1,\dots,K\}$, the rewards $(X_{a,t})_{t\geq 1}$ are independent and bounded in $\Theta = [0,1]$ with common expectation $\mu_a$.

settings.definition_quote: we will assume in this section that, for each arm $a$, the distribution of rewards belongs to a \emph{canonical exponential family}, i.e., that its density with respect to some reference measure can be written as $p_{\theta_a}(x)$ ... $p_{\theta}(x) = \exp\left( x\theta - b(\theta) + c(x) \right)$

algorithms.name: UCB tuned with exploration log(t)+c log log(t)

source.label: th:borneRegret
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem with $K$ arms and independent rewards bounded in $[0,1]$, and denote by $a^*$ an optimal arm. Choosing $c=3$, the regret of the KL-UCB algorithm satisfies: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: d is the Bernoulli KL, so d(mu_a,mu*) = kl_i. Regret derived from expected pull counts, hence pseudo-regret. Corollary 3 notes this is asymptotically optimal for Bernoulli rewards (matches Lai-Robbins). Remark: holds for any c>=3.

symbols.C_1: positive constant (C'_1 <= 7 part from the proof)
symbols.C_2: positive function C_2(epsilon) of epsilon (and the instance), O(epsilon^-2)

source.label: th:borneNbplayed
source.quote: Consider a bandit problem with $K$ arms and independent rewards bounded in $[0,1]$. Let $\epsilon>0$, and take $c=3$ in Algorithm~\ref{alg:klUCB}. ... For any positive integer $n$, the number of times algorithm KL-UCB chooses arm $a$ is upper-bounded by \[\E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}\;,\]

results.notes: Bound on expected number of pulls of a suboptimal arm (quantity 'other'). C_2 and beta depend on the instance too (via d(r(eps),mu_a)).
Asymptotic pull-count bound for a suboptimal arm.

tuning: index S[a]/N[a] + sqrt((log(t)+c log log(t))/(2 N[a]))

source.label: prop:betterUCB
source.quote: Consider the UCB algorithm tuned as follows: at step $t>K$, the arm that maximizes the upper-bound $S[a]/N[a] + \sqrt{(\log(t)+c\log\log(t))/(2 N[a])}$ is chosen. Then, for the choice $c=3$, the number of draws of a sub-optimal arm $a$ is upper-bounded as: \E[N_n(a)] \leq \frac{\log(n)}{2(\mu_a-\mu_{a^*})^2}(1+\epsilon) + C_1 \log(\log(n)) + \frac{C_2(\epsilon)}{n^{\beta(\epsilon)}}

results.notes: Proof omitted in paper (mimics KL-UCB proof with quadratic divergence). Epsilon is quantified implicitly. Proposition number not printed in source.

conditions: rewards of each arm follow the same canonical exponential family with twice differentiable log-partition b
tuning: divergence d replaced by the exponential-family rate function

source.quote: Then, all the results stated above apply (as the proofs do not involve the particular form of the function $d$), and in particular~: \[\limsup_{n\to\infty} \frac{\E[R_n]}{\log(n)} \leq \sum_{a:\mu_a<\mu_{a^*}} \frac{\mu_{a^*}-\mu_a}{d(\mu_a, \mu_{a^*})}\;.\]

results.notes: Stated in prose rather than a formal theorem; by Lemma 4, d(mu_a,mu*) equals KL(p_theta_a, p_theta*), so KL_i. Matches Lai-Robbins for these families. Relies on Theorem 9 whose proof is omitted.

_verify.summary: The extraction is accurate. Theorems 1 and 2, Proposition prop:betterUCB and the Section 4 exponential-family claim are all mapped correctly to canonical variables (kl_i, KL_i, Delta_i) with the right tuning (c=3). Corollary 3 restates the Lai-Robbins optimality comparison and is reasonably mentioned only in the notes. The cited results are recorded as the paper states them.
